# Agent Compactor

Deterministic Node script that splits bloated agent `.md` files into a small **core** (loaded by the SDK on every dispatch) and a set of **on-demand skill files** (loaded by the LLM via `Read` when task keywords match).

## Why

Agent bodies grew to 3k–5k lines. The Claude Agent SDK loads the entire body into the system prompt at dispatch, so every run paid for all of it. A typical run was ~40k tokens of preamble before any work started. Compacting a 5,206-line Koda to a ~400-line core cuts that cost by 70–85% per run. Skills are loaded only when the task actually needs them.

## Quick start

```bash
# Dry-run (prints plan, no writes)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda

# Write to ./.compactor-staging/ for review
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --staging

# Apply to real paths (atomic)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write

# Every agent at once
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all              # dry-run
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write      # apply
```

## How it decides what to split

Six heuristics, applied in order, stopping when the body is under budget:

1. **H1 — topic sections** (`## Billing`, `## Auth`, etc.) → `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`
2. **H2 — protocol bloat** (long `## Protocol`, `## Checklist`) → `skills/<agent>/…-protocol.md`
3. **H3 — large example blocks** (code fences > 40 lines) → `skills/<agent>/examples/<hash>.md`
4. **H4 — tool-specific H3 blocks** (`### Shopify`, `### Supabase`) → `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`
5. **H5 — pattern catalogs** (sections with 10+ numbered bullets) → `skills/<agent>/…-patterns.md`
6. **H6 — appendix / FAQ / antipatterns** → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`

Each extracted skill gets auto-indexed **triggers** (heading words + first-paragraph nouns + back-ticked identifiers) that are embedded in the compacted core as a "Skill Library" section. The LLM reads the core, sees the trigger list, and calls `Read` on the matching skill file when the user's prompt matches.

## Budgets

| Agent | Lines | Chars |
|---|---|---|
| Default | 400 | 16,000 |
| Rex, Arya (orchestrators) | 700 | 28,000 |
| Vex, Zeph (lightweight) | 300 | 12,000 |

Override per-run with `--budget-lines N` / `--budget-chars N`.

Rex is special-cased: only H1 + H5 are applied, to avoid splitting the dispatch logic that makes Rex an orchestrator.

## Safety

- **Idempotent.** Re-running on an already-compacted agent is a no-op unless `--force`.
- **Atomic writes.** Core and skills use `.tmp` + `renameSync`.
- **Staging.** `--staging` writes under `./.compactor-staging/` for diff review before touching real paths.
- **No destructive fallback.** If no heuristic matches, the script reports `SKIP` and writes nothing in `--write` mode.
- **Git recovery.** `~/.claude` is typically backed up to GitHub; `git restore` is the rollback.

## Output shape

After compaction, frontmatter gains:

```yaml
skills:
  - id: billing
    path: skills/koda/billing.md
    triggers: [billing, subscription, stripe, checkout, pricing]
    lines: 412
compactor:
  version: 1
  budget_lines: 400
  budget_chars: 16000
  last_compacted: 2026-04-15T00:00:00Z
  original_sha: 9f3a…
  original_lines: 5206
  original_chars: 191872
```

The body gains a `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section at the bottom telling the LLM when to read each skill.

## Verification

```bash
# Line count drops
wc -l ~/.claude/agents/koda.md

# Skill files land under ~/.claude/skills/koda/
find ~/.claude/skills/koda -type f

# Frontmatter manifest is valid YAML
head -50 ~/.claude/agents/koda.md
```

## Rollback

```bash
cd ~/.claude
git diff agents/koda.md
git restore agents/koda.md
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills/koda
```

## Limits

- Heuristics are regex-based. They may mis-extract sections with ambiguous headings. Always `--staging` first on sensitive agents.
- H3 moves large code blocks. If a block's context was critical, its 2-line stub may be too sparse. Review staged output.
- The LLM must actually follow the skill-library instructions. Early runs should spot-check that the model calls `Read` on the right skill for a matching prompt.

# Self-Test of the Compactor — Critical Bug Found

## Context

The user asked me to self-test the compacted agent system because they can't verify quality easily. Before running any real LLM test, I inspected the artifacts on disk and found a **real correctness bug** that would make the system fail quietly.

## The bug

**Koda's Skill Library references only 1 of 31 skill files on disk.**

- `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md'` → **31 files**
- Koda's body `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section → lists **1 entry** (`advanced-patterns`)
- Koda's frontmatter `skills:` manifest → **1 entry**

The first `compact.mjs --write` extracted 30 skills and wrote everything correctly. The second `--all --write` run (that ran across all 29 agents) re-processed Koda's already-compacted body, treated it as a fresh 582-line input, extracted just 1 more skill from the residue, and **overwrote the Skill Library block + frontmatter manifest with only that single skill** — silently orphaning the 30 skill files from the previous run.

Why it wasn't caught earlier:
- `--all --write` reported "PARTIAL" for Koda instead of "OK already compacted" because the body was still over budget on the residue (400 budget, 582 body).
- The existing idempotency guard only early-returns when the body is *already under budget*. When re-running produces more extractions, the new run replaces the manifest instead of merging with the old one.
- The 30 previous skill files remain on disk (orphaned), so nothing visibly broke — but the LLM loading Koda now has no pointer to them.

This is the kind of bug the plan explicitly warned about ("compactor must never silently degrade an agent") but the harness I built didn't catch it because v1 was diff-only, manual-approve. A cumulative regression across two runs slipped through.

## The fix

Two changes to `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` + `scripts/compactor/render.mjs`:

### 1. Merge, don't replace, the skill manifest on re-run

When compacting an agent whose frontmatter already has a `skills:` manifest, the new run must:
- Read the existing manifest.
- Verify each referenced skill file still exists on disk; drop stale entries (missing files).
- Union new extractions with the existing manifest (by `id` — if the same id is extracted again, new content wins; if different, keep both).
- Rebuild the Skill Library block in the body from the merged manifest, not just the new extractions.

### 2. True idempotency on second-pass compaction

When `compactor.last_compacted` is set and the body is already under budget, skip entirely (current behavior).
When `compactor.last_compacted` is set but the body is still over budget, apply heuristics **and merge** — never orphan the previous manifest.
Add an explicit `compactor.skills_on_disk_verified: true` side-effect that checks every manifest path exists after writing.

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [scripts/compactor/render.mjs](scripts/compactor/render.mjs) | `renderArtifacts` takes `existingSkillManifest` and merges it with new `skills`. Emits a `body` whose Skill Library block lists the union. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | Before `renderArtifacts`, read `parsed.data.skills` from the live frontmatter. Filter to paths that still exist. Pass to render as `existingSkillManifest`. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | In `processAgent`, change the status logic so re-running on an already-compacted agent with orphaned skills produces status `MERGE` (not `PARTIAL`), and prints which skills are being re-linked. |

No API changes. No skill files are rewritten — they exist on disk already.

## Recovery for the already-broken state

For Koda (and any agent with orphaned skills right now), one-time script run:

```bash
# Re-run the compactor with the merge logic — it will find the 30 orphaned
# skill files on disk, re-attach them to the manifest + Skill Library block.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write
# Repeat for any other agent. The --all pass is safe to re-run after the fix.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

Alternative rollback if merge logic misbehaves:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills
# Then re-compact in one pass with the fixed compactor.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

## Verification after the fix

1. `grep -c '→ \`~/.claude/skills/koda/' ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` → should equal `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md' | wc -l`.
2. For every agent, the manifest length in frontmatter must equal the skill files on disk under its folder.
3. Re-run `compact.mjs --all --write` twice back-to-back. Second run should report `OK already compacted` for every agent and leave the manifest unchanged.
4. Smoke-test Koda on a real billing-related prompt; verify the model `Read`s `skills/koda/advanced-patterns.md` (the existing single entry currently routes correctly) AND that restoring the full manifest makes the remaining 30 skills routable.

## Why I'm reporting instead of acting

The user asked me to self-test. I found a bug before running any LLM test. Executing a real test against the broken Koda would waste their tokens — the model would only "see" 1 of 31 skills and the test would be misleading on both sides: skills that were meant to trigger won't, and we'd draw wrong conclusions about the routing contract. Fix the manifest first, then test.

# Self-Test of the Compactor — Critical Bug Found

## Context

The user asked me to self-test the compacted agent system because they can't verify quality easily. Before running any real LLM test, I inspected the artifacts on disk and found a **real correctness bug** that would make the system fail quietly.

## The bug

**Koda's Skill Library references only 1 of 31 skill files on disk.**

- `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md'` → **31 files**
- Koda's body `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section → lists **1 entry** (`advanced-patterns`)
- Koda's frontmatter `skills:` manifest → **1 entry**

The first `compact.mjs --write` extracted 30 skills and wrote everything correctly. The second `--all --write` run (that ran across all 29 agents) re-processed Koda's already-compacted body, treated it as a fresh 582-line input, extracted just 1 more skill from the residue, and **overwrote the Skill Library block + frontmatter manifest with only that single skill** — silently orphaning the 30 skill files from the previous run.

Why it wasn't caught earlier:
- `--all --write` reported "PARTIAL" for Koda instead of "OK already compacted" because the body was still over budget on the residue (400 budget, 582 body).
- The existing idempotency guard only early-returns when the body is *already under budget*. When re-running produces more extractions, the new run replaces the manifest instead of merging with the old one.
- The 30 previous skill files remain on disk (orphaned), so nothing visibly broke — but the LLM loading Koda now has no pointer to them.

This is the kind of bug the plan explicitly warned about ("compactor must never silently degrade an agent") but the harness I built didn't catch it because v1 was diff-only, manual-approve. A cumulative regression across two runs slipped through.

## The fix

Two changes to `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` + `scripts/compactor/render.mjs`:

### 1. Merge, don't replace, the skill manifest on re-run

When compacting an agent whose frontmatter already has a `skills:` manifest, the new run must:
- Read the existing manifest.
- Verify each referenced skill file still exists on disk; drop stale entries (missing files).
- Union new extractions with the existing manifest (by `id` — if the same id is extracted again, new content wins; if different, keep both).
- Rebuild the Skill Library block in the body from the merged manifest, not just the new extractions.

### 2. True idempotency on second-pass compaction

When `compactor.last_compacted` is set and the body is already under budget, skip entirely (current behavior).
When `compactor.last_compacted` is set but the body is still over budget, apply heuristics **and merge** — never orphan the previous manifest.
Add an explicit `compactor.skills_on_disk_verified: true` side-effect that checks every manifest path exists after writing.

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [scripts/compactor/render.mjs](scripts/compactor/render.mjs) | `renderArtifacts` takes `existingSkillManifest` and merges it with new `skills`. Emits a `body` whose Skill Library block lists the union. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | Before `renderArtifacts`, read `parsed.data.skills` from the live frontmatter. Filter to paths that still exist. Pass to render as `existingSkillManifest`. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | In `processAgent`, change the status logic so re-running on an already-compacted agent with orphaned skills produces status `MERGE` (not `PARTIAL`), and prints which skills are being re-linked. |

No API changes. No skill files are rewritten — they exist on disk already.

## Recovery for the already-broken state

For Koda (and any agent with orphaned skills right now), one-time script run:

```bash
# Re-run the compactor with the merge logic — it will find the 30 orphaned
# skill files on disk, re-attach them to the manifest + Skill Library block.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write
# Repeat for any other agent. The --all pass is safe to re-run after the fix.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

Alternative rollback if merge logic misbehaves:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills
# Then re-compact in one pass with the fixed compactor.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

## Verification after the fix

1. `grep -c '→ \`~/.claude/skills/koda/' ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` → should equal `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md' | wc -l`.
2. For every agent, the manifest length in frontmatter must equal the skill files on disk under its folder.
3. Re-run `compact.mjs --all --write` twice back-to-back. Second run should report `OK already compacted` for every agent and leave the manifest unchanged.
4. Smoke-test Koda on a real billing-related prompt; verify the model `Read`s `skills/koda/advanced-patterns.md` (the existing single entry currently routes correctly) AND that restoring the full manifest makes the remaining 30 skills routable.

## Why I'm reporting instead of acting

The user asked me to self-test. I found a bug before running any LLM test. Executing a real test against the broken Koda would waste their tokens — the model would only "see" 1 of 31 skills and the test would be misleading on both sides: skills that were meant to trigger won't, and we'd draw wrong conclusions about the routing contract. Fix the manifest first, then test.

**Weak triggers.** Some entries have generic triggers like "check, duplicate, component, names, reference, claude, memory" — these don't meaningfully route anything because half those words (check, claude, memory, reference) would match almost any task. The heading displayed to the LLM misrepresents the file.

**Found the root cause.** The skill file starts with `## Advanced Patterns` on line 1 — that's an H2, matches correctly. BUT — **inside the file there's a shell-script comment `# Check for duplicate component names` which starts a line with `# ` — matching my H1 regex `/^#\s+/m`!**

**Honest finding: routing is noisy.** For a "Stripe checkout" task, the top candidates by keyword match are:
1. **Shopify Extension Build Patterns** (2 hits: checkout, payment) — **wrong context**, user wants Stripe not Shopify
2. DEEP FORM PATTERNS, DEEP SECURITY PATTERNS, Completion Proof Protocol — all tangentially relevant but none of them are the actual "how to implement Stripe checkout" file
3. Advanced Patterns, Examples — "form" is so generic it matches everything

**The real problem: Koda's original file didn't have a dedicated "## Billing" or "## Stripe" or "## Dodo Payments" section**. So when my compactor split by H2 heading, there was no "Billing" skill to create. The content about billing is scattered across Examples, Deep Security, Completion Proof, etc.

That's where the actual billing info lives.

So **the compactor contract is working correctly**. Billing wasn't in Koda's own content — it lives in memory patterns, which are referenced in the first-load block that's always in the core.

## Self-test report — honest findings

**Bugs found and fixed** during self-test (before any LLM would run):

1. **Critical: Orphaned manifests.** Koda had 31 skill files on disk but only 1 in the Skill Library block. Cause: `--all --write` after individual `--write` runs overwrote the manifest instead of merging. **Fixed.** Added `mergeManifests` in render.mjs, `reconcileManifestFromDisk` + `RECONCILE` mode in compact.mjs, and a `bodyOutOfSync` detector that forces a rewrite even when no new extraction happens.
2. **Bad headings.** Koda's "Advanced Patterns" skill was advertised as "Check for duplicate component names" because my heading extractor was reading `# ...` shell comments inside code fences. **Fixed.** Heading extractor now respects code fences and scans for the first real Markdown heading outside them.
3. **Weak triggers.** Many entries had only generic triggers (claude/memory/patterns/load). **Fixed.** Hydrator now adds domain keywords (billing/stripe/auth/migration/rls/zod/etc.) found in the first 2KB of each skill file.
4. **SKIP path dropped frontmatter fixes.** When a no-progress run still needed manifest repair, the writer short-circuited. **Fixed.** Added `needsRewrite` bypass.

**After fixes:**
- `--all --write` → 26 real agents all clean (disk count = frontmatter count = body count = 1 Skill Library block).
- Idempotent: back-to-back runs produce identical output.
- 32 of 32 Koda skills properly advertised with accurate headings.

**Honest limitation I discovered.** The compactor splits along **structural boundaries** (H2 headings, long protocols, code blocks, pattern catalogs), not along **domain boundaries** (billing/auth/deploy). Koda's source body doesn't have a dedicated `## Billing` section — billing content is scattered inside Examples, Deep Security, Completion Proof, etc. So a "Add Stripe checkout" prompt wouldn't cleanly route to a billing skill (there isn't one). It would route to the closest structural neighbor (Shopify Extensions matched `checkout`+`payment` — wrong context).

The first-load manifest does still reference `memory/patterns/good/billing-patterns.md` directly, so billing knowledge is reachable; it's just not in a Koda-local skill file.

content.text:
## Step 1 — Content-loss audit

The most dangerous failure mode. Before changing anything, I need hard evidence that no content was silently dropped. I'll diff: for each agent, the **original body** should equal the **union of (compacted core body + all its skill files)**, after normalizing whitespace and stripping injected stub/pointer lines.

input.command:
python3 <<'PY'
"""Content-loss audit: verify no original content was dropped during compaction.
For each agent, compute:
    original_body_nonempty  = set of non-empty, non-heading lines in the pre-compact backup
    new_union_nonempty      = set of non-empty, non-heading lines in the compacted core + all its skills
Any line in original but not new_union is a potential content loss.
Stubs/pointers inserted by the compactor are ignored.
"""
import os, re, glob
from pathlib import Path

HOME = os.path.expanduser('~')
BACKUP = f'{HOME}/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15'
AGENTS = f'{HOME}/.claude/agents'
SKILLS = f'{HOME}/.claude/skills'

STUB_RES = [
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*skill:.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*example:.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*tool-guide:.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*Full content moved to.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*Full protocol moved to.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*\d+\s*patterns moved to.*-->'),
    re.compile(r'<!--\s*\d+\s*rules moved to.*-->'),
]
SKILL_REF_RE = re.compile(r'^- \*\*[^*]+\*\* — triggers: _[^_]+_ → `~/\.claude/skills/')
SKILL_LIB_HEADER = re.compile(r'^## Skill Library')

def strip_frontmatter(text):
    m = re.match(r'^---\n[\s\S]*?\n---\n', text)
    return text[m.end():] if m else text

def non_empty_content_lines(text):
    out = []
    in_skill_lib = False
    in_fence = False
    for line in text.split('\n'):
        if SKILL_LIB_HEADER.match(line):
            in_skill_lib = True
            continue
        if in_skill_lib:
            # Skip until another H2 (Skill Library is always last section)
            if re.match(r'^##\s+[A-Z]', line) and not SKILL_LIB_HEADER.match(line):
                in_skill_lib = False
            else:
                continue
        if any(r.search(line) for r in STUB_RES):
            continue
        if SKILL_REF_RE.match(line):
            continue
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped:
            continue
        # Track fences for informational purposes only
        if stripped.startswith('```'):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        # Normalize: collapse internal whitespace
        norm = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', stripped)
        out.append(norm)
    return out

report = []
totals = {'agents': 0, 'total_missing': 0, 'total_original': 0, 'agents_with_loss': 0}

for backup_file in sorted(glob.glob(f'{BACKUP}/*.md')):
    agent = Path(backup_file).stem
    new_file = f'{AGENTS}/{agent}.md'
    skills_dir = f'{SKILLS}/{agent}'
    if not os.path.exists(new_file):
        continue

    orig = strip_frontmatter(Path(backup_file).read_text())
    new_core = strip_frontmatter(Path(new_file).read_text())
    skill_texts = []
    if os.path.isdir(skills_dir):
        for sf in Path(skills_dir).rglob('*.md'):
            skill_texts.append(sf.read_text())

    orig_lines = non_empty_content_lines(orig)
    new_union_lines = non_empty_content_lines(new_core) + sum((non_empty_content_lines(t) for t in skill_texts), [])
    new_set = set(new_union_lines)
    missing = [l for l in orig_lines if l not in new_set]

    totals['agents'] += 1
    totals['total_original'] += len(orig_lines)
    totals['total_missing'] += len(missing)
    if missing:
        totals['agents_with_loss'] += 1
    pct = 100 * len(missing) / max(1, len(orig_lines))
    report.append((agent, len(orig_lines), len(missing), pct, missing[:5]))

# Sort by loss pct
report.sort(key=lambda r: -r[3])

print(f"{'agent':<12} {'orig':>6} {'miss':>6} {'loss%':>7}")
print('-' * 40)
for agent, n_orig, n_miss, pct, sample in report:
    flag = '  ⚠' if pct > 5 else ''
    print(f'{agent:<12} {n_orig:>6} {n_miss:>6} {pct:>6.1f}%{flag}')

print()
print(f"TOTAL: {totals['total_original']} orig lines, {totals['total_missing']} missing ({100*totals['total_missing']/max(1,totals['total_original']):.1f}%)")
print(f"Agents with any loss: {totals['agents_with_loss']} / {totals['agents']}")
print()
print("=== Top 3 agents by loss — sample missing lines ===")
for agent, n_orig, n_miss, pct, sample in report[:3]:
    if not sample: continue
    print(f'\n[{agent}]')
    for l in sample:
        print(f'  - {l[:120]}')
PY

**Found the bug.** H3 (large example blocks) deleted "Contract Testing" because of how it handled an unclosed fence. Look at the context: the preceding H2 ("Load & Stress Testing Patterns") was extracted and replaced with a stub, **but the stub was inserted in the MIDDLE of an open code fence** (javascript block that started before the H2 boundary). When H3 scans for fences in the remaining body, it sees the leftover ` ```javascript ` opening fence, treats everything until the next ` ``` ` as one giant code block, counts >40 lines, and moves it all to `examples/<hash>.md` — deleting the Contract Testing section along with it. Except H3 didn't move it — it probably dropped it because of my fence-scanning loop bug.

172 is even, so original is balanced. The issue is the **H2 extraction broke the balance** by removing a section that contained fence pairs. Let me look at H2's extraction to confirm: `h2ProtocolBloat` and `h2bBulkLargeSections` both replace a section with a short stub. If the section contained fences, they disappear from the remaining body, breaking the balance for subsequent heuristics.

The **root cause**: the section parser (`parseSections`) tracks fences **within** a section but doesn't verify that sections are fence-balanced. When a section is extracted, its fences go with it, but if the section boundary split a fence pair across sections, both sides break.

Example: section X ends with ``` ```javascript ``` (opens fence), section X+1 has code, closes fence, continues. If X+1 is extracted, the ``` in X is now unclosed in `remaining`.

# Agent Compactor

Deterministic Node script that splits bloated agent `.md` files into a small **core** (loaded by the SDK on every dispatch) and a set of **on-demand skill files** (loaded by the LLM via `Read` when task keywords match).

## Why

Agent bodies grew to 3k–5k lines. The Claude Agent SDK loads the entire body into the system prompt at dispatch, so every run paid for all of it. A typical run was ~40k tokens of preamble before any work started. Compacting a 5,206-line Koda to a ~400-line core cuts that cost by 70–85% per run. Skills are loaded only when the task actually needs them.

## Quick start

```bash
# Dry-run (prints plan, no writes)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda

# Write to ./.compactor-staging/ for review
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --staging

# Apply to real paths (atomic)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write

# Every agent at once
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all              # dry-run
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write      # apply
```

## How it decides what to split

Six heuristics, applied in order, stopping when the body is under budget:

1. **H1 — topic sections** (`## Billing`, `## Auth`, etc.) → `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`
2. **H2 — protocol bloat** (long `## Protocol`, `## Checklist`) → `skills/<agent>/…-protocol.md`
3. **H3 — large example blocks** (code fences > 40 lines) → `skills/<agent>/examples/<hash>.md`
4. **H4 — tool-specific H3 blocks** (`### Shopify`, `### Supabase`) → `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`
5. **H5 — pattern catalogs** (sections with 10+ numbered bullets) → `skills/<agent>/…-patterns.md`
6. **H6 — appendix / FAQ / antipatterns** → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`

Each extracted skill gets auto-indexed **triggers** (heading words + first-paragraph nouns + back-ticked identifiers) that are embedded in the compacted core as a "Skill Library" section. The LLM reads the core, sees the trigger list, and calls `Read` on the matching skill file when the user's prompt matches.

## Budgets

| Agent | Lines | Chars |
|---|---|---|
| Default | 400 | 16,000 |
| Rex, Arya (orchestrators) | 700 | 28,000 |
| Vex, Zeph (lightweight) | 300 | 12,000 |

Override per-run with `--budget-lines N` / `--budget-chars N`.

## Continuous operation

### One-time full rebuild
```bash
# From a clean slate (rare — only when heuristics change materially)
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills/*/

```

### Daily / on-demand
```bash
# Auto-compact in the background as you edit agents
node scripts/compactor/watch.mjs
```

### Verify at any time
```bash
node scripts/compactor/verify.mjs                 # default 1% tolerance
node scripts/compactor/verify.mjs --tolerance=0   # zero-loss audit
```

Exit code 0 = clean. Exit code 1 = at least one agent over tolerance (prints offenders + sample missing lines).

## Lifecycle contract

For every agent edit — human or agent-driven:

1. **Edit** the `.md` body as if it were a normal markdown file.
2. **Save** — either:
   - `watch.mjs` is running → compactor runs automatically, aborts on loss.
   - or manually → run `compact.mjs <agent> --write`.
3. **Fail-safe** — if content-loss exceeds tolerance, the write is aborted and the agent file is left untouched. Fix the input (or tune heuristics), re-run.

### When adding a new agent
1. Write the full-size `.md` under `~/.claude/agents/<id>.md`.
2. Run `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs <id> --staging` — inspect planned skill files.
3. Run `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs <id> --write` — real apply.
4. `verify.mjs` confirms zero loss.

### When editing an existing agent
- **Small edits** (< 5% of body): watch-mode or `--write` handles the rest; if body shrinks under budget, no re-extraction is needed.
- **Major rewrites** (>20% changes): consider `--reconcile --write` to rebuild the Skill Library block and trigger set from current skill files on disk.
- **Adding a section** that should become its own skill: give it a distinct H2 heading matching one of the H1 keywords (`billing`, `auth`, `migration`, etc.) OR make it >150 lines so H2b catches it.

### When removing a skill file manually
- Delete `~/.claude/skills/<agent>/<file>.md`.
- Re-run `compact.mjs <agent> --reconcile --write` to sync the frontmatter manifest and Skill Library block.

### When renaming/moving a skill
- Don't. The compactor regenerates filenames deterministically from headings. Rename the source H2 heading in the agent's `.md`; on next compaction the skill file is recreated under the new name and the old one is orphaned (safe to delete).

## Heuristics (in order)

1. **H1 — topic sections** (`## Billing`, `## Auth`, …) → dedicated skill file.
2. **H2 — protocol/rules/patterns bloat** (`## DEEP X PATTERNS`, `## Premium UI/UX Standards`) → dedicated skill.
3. **H4 — tool-specific H3 blocks** (`### Shopify`, `### Supabase`) → `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`.
4. **H5 — pattern catalogs** (sections with 10+ numbered bullets) → dedicated skill.
5. **H6 — appendix / FAQ / antipatterns** → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`.
6. **H3 — large balanced code fences** (>40 lines, ≤500 lines, no embedded headings) → `skills/<agent>/examples/<hash>.md`.
7. **H2b — any remaining H2 >150 lines** → dedicated skill (last-resort bulk extractor).

**Safety rails built into heuristics:**
- H2/H2b stubs are **fence-free** — never excerpt content that might open a code fence the rest of the pipeline can't close.
- H3 refuses to extract unclosed or heading-spanning fences — leaves them in the core verbatim.
- Dedupe is by skill `id` (content-hash for examples, slug for sections), not by heading — multiple example blocks don't collapse.

# Agent Compactor — Production Lifecycle

> **Safety contract (hard):** No agent write is allowed if content-loss exceeds tolerance (default 1%, enforced as `ABORT` status). Every Markdown line from the original body must exist in either the compacted core or a skill file. Enforced by `verify.mjs` both at pre-write time and as a standalone audit.



Deterministic Node script that splits bloated agent `.md` files into a small **core** (loaded by the SDK on every dispatch) and a set of **on-demand skill files** (loaded by the LLM via `Read` when task keywords match).

## Why

Agent bodies grew to 3k–5k lines. The Claude Agent SDK loads the entire body into the system prompt at dispatch, so every run paid for all of it. A typical run was ~40k tokens of preamble before any work started. Compacting a 5,206-line Koda to a ~400-line core cuts that cost by 70–85% per run. Skills are loaded only when the task actually needs them.

## Quick start

```bash
# Dry-run (prints plan, no writes)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda

# Write to ./.compactor-staging/ for review
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --staging

# Apply to real paths (atomic)
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write

# Every agent at once
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all              # dry-run
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write      # apply
```

## How it decides what to split

Six heuristics, applied in order, stopping when the body is under budget:

1. **H1 — topic sections** (`## Billing`, `## Auth`, etc.) → `skills/<agent>/<slug>.md`
2. **H2 — protocol bloat** (long `## Protocol`, `## Checklist`) → `skills/<agent>/…-protocol.md`
3. **H3 — large example blocks** (code fences > 40 lines) → `skills/<agent>/examples/<hash>.md`
4. **H4 — tool-specific H3 blocks** (`### Shopify`, `### Supabase`) → `skills/<agent>/tools/<tool>.md`
5. **H5 — pattern catalogs** (sections with 10+ numbered bullets) → `skills/<agent>/…-patterns.md`
6. **H6 — appendix / FAQ / antipatterns** → `skills/<agent>/reference.md`

Each extracted skill gets auto-indexed **triggers** (heading words + first-paragraph nouns + back-ticked identifiers) that are embedded in the compacted core as a "Skill Library" section. The LLM reads the core, sees the trigger list, and calls `Read` on the matching skill file when the user's prompt matches.

content.text:
Refresh the Agents page — every row now shows a colored heart-icon health pill next to the level/experience badges.

**What shipped:**

- [src/health.js](src/health.js) — deterministic 0–100 score from 3 signal sources (`agent_runs`, `witness_log`, `daily_scores`), plus registry status penalty. Single batched query for all agents, zero per-row round trips.
- [src/server.js](src/server.js) `/api/unified/agents` — batch-computes health, attaches `health` field to every row.
- [client/src/types.ts](client/src/types.ts) — `AgentHealth` type + `UnifiedAgent.health` field.
- [client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx](client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx) — new `HealthBadge` component, inline on the main row next to the other badges. Hover for a breakdown tooltip.

**Scoring formula (transparent):**
```
score = 100
  - min(40, failures × 4)       # max 40
  - min(30, antipatterns × 6)   # max 30
  - min(20, regressions × 10)   # max 20
  - statusPenalty                # pip -20, probation -10, retired -50
  - 10 if last run > 30 days ago
band: ≥80 healthy (green) | 60-79 warn (amber) | <60 action (red)
```

**Cold-start behavior:** agents with no 14-day data get a neutral **85 green** with "new — no recent run data" in the tooltip — they don't look failing just because they haven't run yet.

**Current distribution:** 30/30 healthy (29 cold, 1 with a real successful Scout run → 100).

As real runs accumulate (from `agent_runs` and Witness daily sweeps), scores auto-update on every page load — no cron needed. The badge color moves down toward amber/red when failures/antipatterns/regressions accrue; hovering shows exactly why.

Decoded honestly — 7.6k tokens for one agent definition is on the heavy side, but the real question isn't "is 7.6k a lot" in isolation; it's "what's the cost across 30 agents × N runs/week, and is the file actually earning its weight?"

**The math that matters**

At ~$0.137/run shown in your screenshot, that's just the *agent definition load* — before any actual work. If Mira runs ~20 times/week (post-build sweeps + weekly auto-sweep + ad-hoc), that's ~$2.74/week just to load Mira's instructions. Across 30 agents at similar bloat, you're looking at $80–100/week in pure context-loading overhead before a single line of useful work. Annualized: ~$4–5k just to tell agents who they are.

More important than dollars: **context dilution is a real performance hit**. Research on long-context LLMs is consistent — instruction-following degrades as system prompts balloon, especially past 5–6k tokens. Your agent is at 7.6k of instructions before it sees the actual task. Your 642 lines almost certainly contain rules that get ignored under load.

**Pros of the current Mira file**

It's comprehensive — self-validation, auto-fix loop, smart defaults, escalation triggers, conflict resolution, pattern quality scoring, anti-patterns list, git autonomy rules. Mira knows what to do without asking. The "Skill Library" pattern at the bottom shows you've already started routing heavy content to on-demand loads. The first-load manifest is well-designed.

**Cons (the real problems)**

1. **Massive duplication from training updates layered on top of each other.** You have "Training 2026-04-11", "Training 2026-04-11 (b)", "Training 2026-04-11 (c)", "DEEP TRAINING 2026-04-10", "DEEP TRAINING 2026-04-14", "STACK A MIGRATION 2026-04-10". Each one re-states mandatory loads, smart defaults, auto-fix loops, escalation rules. The same concepts appear 3–4 times in slightly different wording. This is the single biggest bloat source.

2. **Anti-patterns + Standards + Completion Criteria + Quality Scoring overlap heavily** with `universal-auto-fix-loop.md` and `validation-gates.md` that already load externally. You're paying tokens for both the reference *and* a paraphrased version inline.

3. **Templates (Retrospective Framework, Training Report Output, Velocity tracking) are inline** — these are reference templates Mira uses occasionally, not every run. Classic skill candidates.

4. **The bottom Skill Library proves the pattern works** — you already moved 6 sections out. The remaining bloat is everything that *should* have been moved but wasn't.

5. **400-line budget you set is reasonable**; 642 lines is your own system flagging this exact problem. Trust the alarm.

**Recommended actions, ranked by ROI**

*Highest impact (do this week):*

Consolidate the four "Training 2026-04-11 (a/b/c)" + "DEEP TRAINING" + "STACK A MIGRATION" sections into ONE canonical section called "Active Protocols" with bullet refs to the skill files. Kill the dated headers — git log is your audit trail, not the agent file. **Estimated cut: 180–220 lines.**

*High impact:*

Move to skills (load-on-demand): Retrospective Framework, Training Report Output template, Pattern Promotion Rules, Memory Maintenance Schedule, Conflict Resolution Framework, Pattern Quality Scoring rubric, Knowledge Graph Maintenance, Mira Anti-Patterns Top 10, Bug clustering algorithm + stale-check Python. **Estimated cut: 200+ lines.**

Keep inline ONLY: role definition, first-load manifest (Tier 1/2), completion criteria checklist, escalation triggers, the skill library router. That's the irreducible core.

*Medium impact:*

The "Mandatory loads at start of every run" appears 3+ times. Pick one location, delete the rest.

The Claude Hub Learning System Integration code blocks — move the JS examples to a skill, keep only "Mira pulls learning data via Claude Hub API after each cycle" inline.

*Strategic question worth answering before refactoring:*

Mira is doing four jobs: extracting patterns, maintaining memory health, tracking agent performance, and running weekly sweeps. That's why the file is bloated. Two options:

- **Compact and keep monolithic** → target ~280 lines, push everything else to skills
- **Split into sub-agents** → Mira-Extractor (per-build), Mira-Sweeper (weekly), Mira-Performance (analytics). Each ~200 lines, loaded only when needed

Given you have 30 agents already, I'd lean toward **compact, don't split** — adding more agents has its own management overhead, and Mira's jobs are tightly related. Aim for 250–300 lines, ~12K chars, ~3k tokens. That cuts your per-run cost by ~60% and gets you back inside the budget you set.

One more thing worth flagging — if all 30 agents are at similar bloat, run the same audit across the squad. The fix pattern is identical (consolidate dated training notes, move templates and rubrics to skills, dedupe mandatory loads). A 2-hour cleanup pass across the squad probably saves you $3–4k/year and noticeably improves instruction adherence.

content.text:
## Honest verdict on the advice + what I did

**The advice was right on the substance, wrong on the response.** "Do a 2-hour cleanup pass" is the wrong frame — manual cleanup doesn't scale and decays. The right response is to **teach the compactor to recognize the bloat patterns it was missing** so the problem self-heals for every future agent.

**Verified claims before acting:**
- Mira really had 7 dated training sections (86+86+66+49+46+24+17 = ~370 lines). ✓
- "MANDATORY" appears 7×, "auto-fix" 11× — real duplication. ✓
- 22 of 29 agents were still over budget before this pass. ✓
- The first-load manifest *was* duplicated in Mira (appears 2× as a header, but "mandatory loads" rules are restated in multiple training sections). ✓

**What I shipped:**

Two new heuristics in [scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs](scripts/compactor/heuristics.mjs):

- **H7 — dated-training-archaeology extractor.** Matches `## Training YYYY-MM-DD`, `## DEEP TRAINING YYYY-MM-DD`, `## TRAINING UPDATE YYYY-MM-DD`, `## STACK X MIGRATION YYYY-MM-DD`, `## ★ DEEP TRAINING`, etc. Bundles them into a single `skills/<agent>/training-history.md` — searchable, loadable on demand, **keeps all content** (it's audit-trail material, not trash).
- **H8 — templates + rubrics extractor.** Matches "Retrospective Framework", "Training Report Output", "Anti-Patterns (Top N)", "Memory Maintenance Schedule", "Pattern Promotion Rules", "Pattern Quality Scoring", "Conflict Resolution Framework", "Knowledge Graph Maintenance", "High-Value Training Categories", "Bug Clustering". Bundles into `skills/<agent>/templates-and-rubrics.md`.

**Results:**

| Metric | Before this pass | After this pass |
|---|---|---|
| Agents under budget (OK) | 8 | **17** |
| Agents over budget | 22 | 12 |
| Total agent-body lines | 16,481 | **12,898 (-22%)** |
| Mira specifically | 642 lines, 7.6k tokens | **223 lines, ~2.7k tokens (-65%)** |

# Self-Test of the Compactor — Critical Bug Found

## Context

The user asked me to self-test the compacted agent system because they can't verify quality easily. Before running any real LLM test, I inspected the artifacts on disk and found a **real correctness bug** that would make the system fail quietly.

## The bug

**Koda's Skill Library references only 1 of 31 skill files on disk.**

- `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md'` → **31 files**
- Koda's body `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section → lists **1 entry** (`advanced-patterns`)
- Koda's frontmatter `skills:` manifest → **1 entry**

The first `compact.mjs --write` extracted 30 skills and wrote everything correctly. The second `--all --write` run (that ran across all 29 agents) re-processed Koda's already-compacted body, treated it as a fresh 582-line input, extracted just 1 more skill from the residue, and **overwrote the Skill Library block + frontmatter manifest with only that single skill** — silently orphaning the 30 skill files from the previous run.

Why it wasn't caught earlier:
- `--all --write` reported "PARTIAL" for Koda instead of "OK already compacted" because the body was still over budget on the residue (400 budget, 582 body).
- The existing idempotency guard only early-returns when the body is *already under budget*. When re-running produces more extractions, the new run replaces the manifest instead of merging with the old one.
- The 30 previous skill files remain on disk (orphaned), so nothing visibly broke — but the LLM loading Koda now has no pointer to them.

This is the kind of bug the plan explicitly warned about ("compactor must never silently degrade an agent") but the harness I built didn't catch it because v1 was diff-only, manual-approve. A cumulative regression across two runs slipped through.

## The fix

Two changes to `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` + `scripts/compactor/render.mjs`:

### 1. Merge, don't replace, the skill manifest on re-run

When compacting an agent whose frontmatter already has a `skills:` manifest, the new run must:
- Read the existing manifest.
- Verify each referenced skill file still exists on disk; drop stale entries (missing files).
- Union new extractions with the existing manifest (by `id` — if the same id is extracted again, new content wins; if different, keep both).
- Rebuild the Skill Library block in the body from the merged manifest, not just the new extractions.

### 2. True idempotency on second-pass compaction

When `compactor.last_compacted` is set and the body is already under budget, skip entirely (current behavior).
When `compactor.last_compacted` is set but the body is still over budget, apply heuristics **and merge** — never orphan the previous manifest.
Add an explicit `compactor.skills_on_disk_verified: true` side-effect that checks every manifest path exists after writing.

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [scripts/compactor/render.mjs](scripts/compactor/render.mjs) | `renderArtifacts` takes `existingSkillManifest` and merges it with new `skills`. Emits a `body` whose Skill Library block lists the union. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | Before `renderArtifacts`, read `parsed.data.skills` from the live frontmatter. Filter to paths that still exist. Pass to render as `existingSkillManifest`. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | In `processAgent`, change the status logic so re-running on an already-compacted agent with orphaned skills produces status `MERGE` (not `PARTIAL`), and prints which skills are being re-linked. |

No API changes. No skill files are rewritten — they exist on disk already.

## Recovery for the already-broken state

For Koda (and any agent with orphaned skills right now), one-time script run:

```bash
# Re-run the compactor with the merge logic — it will find the 30 orphaned
# skill files on disk, re-attach them to the manifest + Skill Library block.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write
# Repeat for any other agent. The --all pass is safe to re-run after the fix.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

Alternative rollback if merge logic misbehaves:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills
# Then re-compact in one pass with the fixed compactor.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

## Verification after the fix

1. `grep -c '→ \`~/.claude/skills/koda/' ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` → should equal `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md' | wc -l`.
2. For every agent, the manifest length in frontmatter must equal the skill files on disk under its folder.
3. Re-run `compact.mjs --all --write` twice back-to-back. Second run should report `OK already compacted` for every agent and leave the manifest unchanged.
4. Smoke-test Koda on a real billing-related prompt; verify the model `Read`s `skills/koda/advanced-patterns.md` (the existing single entry currently routes correctly) AND that restoring the full manifest makes the remaining 30 skills routable.

## Why I'm reporting instead of acting

The user asked me to self-test. I found a bug before running any LLM test. Executing a real test against the broken Koda would waste their tokens — the model would only "see" 1 of 31 skills and the test would be misleading on both sides: skills that were meant to trigger won't, and we'd draw wrong conclusions about the routing contract. Fix the manifest first, then test.

Now I see the issue. The list row (`/api/unified/agents`) and the editor health bar (`/api/agents/:name/health`) both use `checkBudget()` but there's a key difference:

**List row**: `computeBudgetHealth` uses `agent.raw` — which is the **full raw file including frontmatter**.
**Editor health bar**: `checkBudget({ agentId, content: raw })` — also reads the full file.

But the list endpoint only loads `agent.raw` if the meta-only mode doesn't strip it. Let me check what `getUnifiedAgents` actually returns for the `raw` field.

Found the root cause.

`/api/unified/agents` calls `listAgents()` (line 1108) which uses `parseAgent()` — that includes the full `raw` field. So `computeBudgetHealth` gets `agent.raw` correctly.

But the **editor health bar** (`AgentHealthBar`) calls `/api/agents/:name/health` which reads the file fresh from disk and passes `content: raw` to `checkBudget()`. That `raw` is the **full file including frontmatter**.

The list row's `computeBudgetHealth` also passes `agent.raw` (full file including frontmatter) to `checkBudget()`.

So they should match. Let me check `checkBudget` — does it use the full raw or strip frontmatter first?

Good — `checkBudget` correctly strips frontmatter via `splitFrontmatter` and measures only the body. So both endpoints pass the same full raw content and `checkBudget` handles the split identically. The budget numbers should match.

Now let me check the **client-side** — `AgentHealthBar` calls `getAgentHealth` which posts to a different endpoint. Let me verify the API client:

- `agent.raw` = same full file content

content.text:
**Critical bug found.**

`parseFrontmatter` parses YAML line by line with a simple `colonIdx` split. This means **multi-line YAML values** (like `skills:` which is a YAML list) get mangled or lost. For compacted agents with a `skills:` block in frontmatter like:

```yaml
---
skills:
  - id: billing
    path: ~/.claude/skills/koda/billing.md
    trigger: billing
compactor:
  last_compacted: 2026-04-10
  budget_lines: 400
---
```

The `parseFrontmatter` only captures flat `key: value` lines — multi-line values like the `skills:` list are parsed as individual orphaned lines (e.g. `id: billing`, `path: ...`) OR dropped entirely. Then `serializeAgent` reconstructs from only the captured flat meta, **stripping the `compactor:` block and `skills:` list**.

So the editor health bar gets `content` = a file **without** the `compactor.budget_lines` override. This means `checkBudget` falls back to the **default budget** (400 lines) instead of the agent's custom budget. The list uses `agent.raw` (full file, correct YAML parsed by `gray-matter`), so `checkBudget` gets the `compactor.budget_lines` override correctly.

This is why the scores differ — the budgets used are different.

The fix: `AgentHealthBar` should call the health endpoint **without** the `content` prop when it's rendering the on-disk state (not live editing). When the user is actively editing, pass content. But the simpler correct fix for the initial load: pass `content={getCurrentRaw()}` only when the user has made edits (`dirty`), otherwise let the endpoint read from disk.

## Graphify Analysis Report

**1. Core Functionality**
Graphify transforms unstructured file collections (code, docs, PDFs, images, videos) into interactive, queryable knowledge graphs. It extracts relationships and structure automatically, enabling users to discover connections they didn't know existed.

**2. Tech Stack**
- **Graph processing**: NetworkX, Leiden clustering (graspologic), vis.js visualization
- **Code analysis**: tree-sitter AST parsing for 25+ languages
- **Media processing**: faster-whisper (local transcription), yt-dlp (video downloads), Claude vision
- **Model backends**: Claude API, GPT-4, platform-specific models (Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Gemini, Aider)
- **Export**: JSON, HTML, Markdown, GraphML, Neo4j Cypher, Obsidian vaults

**3. Problem Solved**
Eliminates information overload in research/development workflows. Users often accumulate hundreds of unorganized files. Graphify dramatically reduces token consumption (71.5x improvement) while maintaining persistent, reusable knowledge across sessions—inspired by researchers collecting papers in `/raw` folders.

**4. Key Features**
- Multimodal input processing (code, docs, PDFs, images, videos)

# Self-Test of the Compactor — Critical Bug Found

## Context

The user asked me to self-test the compacted agent system because they can't verify quality easily. Before running any real LLM test, I inspected the artifacts on disk and found a **real correctness bug** that would make the system fail quietly.

## The bug

**Koda's Skill Library references only 1 of 31 skill files on disk.**

- `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md'` → **31 files**
- Koda's body `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section → lists **1 entry** (`advanced-patterns`)
- Koda's frontmatter `skills:` manifest → **1 entry**

The first `compact.mjs --write` extracted 30 skills and wrote everything correctly. The second `--all --write` run (that ran across all 29 agents) re-processed Koda's already-compacted body, treated it as a fresh 582-line input, extracted just 1 more skill from the residue, and **overwrote the Skill Library block + frontmatter manifest with only that single skill** — silently orphaning the 30 skill files from the previous run.

Why it wasn't caught earlier:
- `--all --write` reported "PARTIAL" for Koda instead of "OK already compacted" because the body was still over budget on the residue (400 budget, 582 body).
- The existing idempotency guard only early-returns when the body is *already under budget*. When re-running produces more extractions, the new run replaces the manifest instead of merging with the old one.
- The 30 previous skill files remain on disk (orphaned), so nothing visibly broke — but the LLM loading Koda now has no pointer to them.

This is the kind of bug the plan explicitly warned about ("compactor must never silently degrade an agent") but the harness I built didn't catch it because v1 was diff-only, manual-approve. A cumulative regression across two runs slipped through.

## The fix

Two changes to `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` + `scripts/compactor/render.mjs`:

### 1. Merge, don't replace, the skill manifest on re-run

When compacting an agent whose frontmatter already has a `skills:` manifest, the new run must:
- Read the existing manifest.
- Verify each referenced skill file still exists on disk; drop stale entries (missing files).
- Union new extractions with the existing manifest (by `id` — if the same id is extracted again, new content wins; if different, keep both).
- Rebuild the Skill Library block in the body from the merged manifest, not just the new extractions.

### 2. True idempotency on second-pass compaction

When `compactor.last_compacted` is set and the body is already under budget, skip entirely (current behavior).
When `compactor.last_compacted` is set but the body is still over budget, apply heuristics **and merge** — never orphan the previous manifest.
Add an explicit `compactor.skills_on_disk_verified: true` side-effect that checks every manifest path exists after writing.

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [scripts/compactor/render.mjs](scripts/compactor/render.mjs) | `renderArtifacts` takes `existingSkillManifest` and merges it with new `skills`. Emits a `body` whose Skill Library block lists the union. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | Before `renderArtifacts`, read `parsed.data.skills` from the live frontmatter. Filter to paths that still exist. Pass to render as `existingSkillManifest`. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | In `processAgent`, change the status logic so re-running on an already-compacted agent with orphaned skills produces status `MERGE` (not `PARTIAL`), and prints which skills are being re-linked. |

No API changes. No skill files are rewritten — they exist on disk already.

## Recovery for the already-broken state

For Koda (and any agent with orphaned skills right now), one-time script run:

```bash
# Re-run the compactor with the merge logic — it will find the 30 orphaned
# skill files on disk, re-attach them to the manifest + Skill Library block.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write
# Repeat for any other agent. The --all pass is safe to re-run after the fix.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

Alternative rollback if merge logic misbehaves:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills
# Then re-compact in one pass with the fixed compactor.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

## Verification after the fix

1. `grep -c '→ \`~/.claude/skills/koda/' ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` → should equal `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md' | wc -l`.
2. For every agent, the manifest length in frontmatter must equal the skill files on disk under its folder.
3. Re-run `compact.mjs --all --write` twice back-to-back. Second run should report `OK already compacted` for every agent and leave the manifest unchanged.
4. Smoke-test Koda on a real billing-related prompt; verify the model `Read`s `skills/koda/advanced-patterns.md` (the existing single entry currently routes correctly) AND that restoring the full manifest makes the remaining 30 skills routable.

## Why I'm reporting instead of acting

The user asked me to self-test. I found a bug before running any LLM test. Executing a real test against the broken Koda would waste their tokens — the model would only "see" 1 of 31 skills and the test would be misleading on both sides: skills that were meant to trigger won't, and we'd draw wrong conclusions about the routing contract. Fix the manifest first, then test.

# Knowledge Graph — Polyglot Agent Intelligence Map

## Context

User wants to implement Graphify's knowledge graph concepts into Polyglot. Graphify turns files into interactive, queryable knowledge graphs with clustering, confidence-scored edges, and physics-based vis.js visualization.

Polyglot already has:
- Full agent graph data via `/api/org-chart` (nodes + edges, all metadata)
- `@xyflow/react` installed and used in an existing OrgChart page
- Skill manifests in agent frontmatter (`skills: [{id, path, lines}]`)
- Computed skill scores in registry (`{ react: { score, hits } }`)
- Org registry with departments, phases, reportsTo hierarchy, levels, tiers

## What we're building

A new **Knowledge Graph page** (`/knowledge-graph`) — a force-directed interactive graph of the entire agent workforce showing:

1. **Agent ↔ Agent edges** (reportsTo hierarchy — already in `/api/org-chart`)
2. **Agent ↔ Skill edges** (from `frontmatter.skills[]` manifest — what skills each agent owns)
3. **Agent ↔ Agent skill-overlap edges** (inferred — agents sharing skill domains get a dashed "collaborates" edge)
4. **Clustering by department** (colored node groups matching existing department colors)
5. **Confidence tagging on edges** — EXTRACTED (solid, reportsTo), INFERRED (dashed, skill overlap)

## Data model (Graphify-inspired)

### Nodes
```typescript
interface GraphNode {
  id: string                    // agent filename (e.g. "rex") or skill id (e.g. "skill:billing")
  type: 'agent' | 'skill'
  label: string                 // display name
  department: string | null
  departmentColor: string
  community: number             // department index (0=largest), used for color
  level: number | null          // agent level 0-6
  tier: string | null
  status: string | null
  degree: number                // computed: number of edges
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>
}
```

### Edges
```typescript
interface GraphEdge {
  id: string
  source: string
  target: string
  relation: 'reports_to' | 'owns_skill' | 'skill_overlap'
  confidence: 'EXTRACTED' | 'INFERRED'
```

# Self-Test of the Compactor — Critical Bug Found

## Context

The user asked me to self-test the compacted agent system because they can't verify quality easily. Before running any real LLM test, I inspected the artifacts on disk and found a **real correctness bug** that would make the system fail quietly.

## The bug

**Koda's Skill Library references only 1 of 31 skill files on disk.**

- `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md'` → **31 files**
- Koda's body `## Skill Library (load on demand)` section → lists **1 entry** (`advanced-patterns`)
- Koda's frontmatter `skills:` manifest → **1 entry**

The first `compact.mjs --write` extracted 30 skills and wrote everything correctly. The second `--all --write` run (that ran across all 29 agents) re-processed Koda's already-compacted body, treated it as a fresh 582-line input, extracted just 1 more skill from the residue, and **overwrote the Skill Library block + frontmatter manifest with only that single skill** — silently orphaning the 30 skill files from the previous run.

Why it wasn't caught earlier:
- `--all --write` reported "PARTIAL" for Koda instead of "OK already compacted" because the body was still over budget on the residue (400 budget, 582 body).
- The existing idempotency guard only early-returns when the body is *already under budget*. When re-running produces more extractions, the new run replaces the manifest instead of merging with the old one.
- The 30 previous skill files remain on disk (orphaned), so nothing visibly broke — but the LLM loading Koda now has no pointer to them.

This is the kind of bug the plan explicitly warned about ("compactor must never silently degrade an agent") but the harness I built didn't catch it because v1 was diff-only, manual-approve. A cumulative regression across two runs slipped through.

## The fix

Two changes to `scripts/compactor/compact.mjs` + `scripts/compactor/render.mjs`:

### 1. Merge, don't replace, the skill manifest on re-run

When compacting an agent whose frontmatter already has a `skills:` manifest, the new run must:
- Read the existing manifest.
- Verify each referenced skill file still exists on disk; drop stale entries (missing files).
- Union new extractions with the existing manifest (by `id` — if the same id is extracted again, new content wins; if different, keep both).
- Rebuild the Skill Library block in the body from the merged manifest, not just the new extractions.

### 2. True idempotency on second-pass compaction

When `compactor.last_compacted` is set and the body is already under budget, skip entirely (current behavior).
When `compactor.last_compacted` is set but the body is still over budget, apply heuristics **and merge** — never orphan the previous manifest.
Add an explicit `compactor.skills_on_disk_verified: true` side-effect that checks every manifest path exists after writing.

## Files to modify

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [scripts/compactor/render.mjs](scripts/compactor/render.mjs) | `renderArtifacts` takes `existingSkillManifest` and merges it with new `skills`. Emits a `body` whose Skill Library block lists the union. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | Before `renderArtifacts`, read `parsed.data.skills` from the live frontmatter. Filter to paths that still exist. Pass to render as `existingSkillManifest`. |
| [scripts/compactor/compact.mjs](scripts/compactor/compact.mjs) | In `processAgent`, change the status logic so re-running on an already-compacted agent with orphaned skills produces status `MERGE` (not `PARTIAL`), and prints which skills are being re-linked. |

No API changes. No skill files are rewritten — they exist on disk already.

## Recovery for the already-broken state

For Koda (and any agent with orphaned skills right now), one-time script run:

```bash
# Re-run the compactor with the merge logic — it will find the 30 orphaned
# skill files on disk, re-attach them to the manifest + Skill Library block.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs koda --write
# Repeat for any other agent. The --all pass is safe to re-run after the fix.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

Alternative rollback if merge logic misbehaves:

```bash
cp ~/.claude/agents/.pre-compact-2026-04-15/*.md ~/.claude/agents/
rm -rf ~/.claude/skills
# Then re-compact in one pass with the fixed compactor.
node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs --all --write
```

## Verification after the fix

1. `grep -c '→ \`~/.claude/skills/koda/' ~/.claude/agents/koda.md` → should equal `find ~/.claude/skills/koda -name '*.md' | wc -l`.
2. For every agent, the manifest length in frontmatter must equal the skill files on disk under its folder.
3. Re-run `compact.mjs --all --write` twice back-to-back. Second run should report `OK already compacted` for every agent and leave the manifest unchanged.
4. Smoke-test Koda on a real billing-related prompt; verify the model `Read`s `skills/koda/advanced-patterns.md` (the existing single entry currently routes correctly) AND that restoring the full manifest makes the remaining 30 skills routable.

## Why I'm reporting instead of acting

The user asked me to self-test. I found a bug before running any LLM test. Executing a real test against the broken Koda would waste their tokens — the model would only "see" 1 of 31 skills and the test would be misleading on both sides: skills that were meant to trigger won't, and we'd draw wrong conclusions about the routing contract. Fix the manifest first, then test.

One issue: `Edge` type is imported but the `rfEdges` array's items have an extra `data` field that TypeScript might flag. Also, the `label` on edges needs to be a `ReactNode` in React Flow — string is fine. Let me check if `Edge` from `@xyflow/react` accepts `data`:

The `Edge` type in `@xyflow/react` is generic: `Edge<T>` where `T` is the data type. We're not specifying it so it defaults to `unknown`. The extra `data: e` field should be fine since React Flow's `Edge` type accepts arbitrary `data`. This won't cause a TS error.

However there's a subtle issue with the `computeLayout` function — the `rfNodes` array holds items with `data: n` where `n` is `KnowledgeGraphNode`, and we typed the array as `Node[]` (without generic). React Flow's `Node` type is `Node<Record<string, unknown>>` by default. Since `KnowledgeGraphNode` satisfies that, it should be fine.

# Cleanup + High-Value Features Plan

## Context

Goal: mass autonomous software production with low token use, no quality compromise.
Current state: Polyglot has solid infrastructure but it's cluttered with dead pages, unused server routes wired to nothing, and the highest-leverage features (smart dispatch, pipeline templates) are either server-side dead code or completely missing.

This plan removes dead weight and adds the 3 highest-ROI features in order.

---

## Phase 1 — Remove dead weight (no-risk, immediate)

### 1A. Remove `HowItWorks` page
- **Why:** 636 lines, reachable only via CommandPalette, zero functional value. It's a tutorial nobody reads.
- **Files:**
  - Delete `client/src/pages/HowItWorks.tsx`
  - Remove import + route from `client/src/App.tsx` (line 30 import, line 74 route `/how-it-works`)
  - Remove from `client/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx` line 56

### 1B. Remove `Knowledge Graph` page + route + sidebar link
- **Why:** 849 lines of pure visualization, zero dispatch, zero token savings, zero production value. The same org/dept info is already in OrgChart. We just built it but it solves no real problem.
- **Files:**
  - Delete `client/src/pages/KnowledgeGraph.tsx`
  - Remove import + route from `client/src/App.tsx`
  - Remove nav link + `Network` icon import from `client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`
  - Remove `GET /api/knowledge-graph` from `src/routes/knowledgeGraph.js` (delete file)
  - Remove `knowledgeGraphRouter` require + `app.use` from `src/server.js`
  - Remove `getKnowledgeGraph`, `KnowledgeGraphNode`, `KnowledgeGraphEdge`, `KnowledgeGraphData` types from `client/src/lib/api.ts`

### 1C. Compact the 2 over-budget agents
- **Why:** `harvest.md` (183 lines, active cron agent) and any audit stub are burning tokens on every load.

### 1D. Remove dead `learning/route` frontend dead-end
- **Why:** `GET /api/learning/route/:taskType` returns smart routing but zero frontend calls it. Either wire it or remove the confusion. We will wire it (Phase 2), so keep the server route — but note it's currently dead.

---

## Phase 2 — Smart Dispatch (highest ROI)

**What:** A task input bar on the Agents page (or a new `/dispatch` panel) where you type a task description → system scores every agent by skill match → shows top 3 agents with confidence % → one-click to open that agent or fire it in Playground.

**Why it matters:** This is the routing brain. Instead of you remembering which agent handles what, the system tells you. Directly cuts the mental overhead of the "who does this?" decision on every task.

### Backend — wire existing `/api/learning/route/:taskType`

The route already exists in `src/routes/learning.js` lines 140-156. It pattern-matches taskType against agent rankings by successRate. We need to enhance it:

- Change from regex taskType lookup to **free-text skill matching** against registry `skills` object (score × hits weighted)
- Input: `?q=build+auth+middleware+for+nextjs`
- Output: top 5 agents ranked by skill overlap score, with matched skills listed

**New endpoint:** `GET /api/dispatch/recommend?q=<free text>`
- Tokenize query into keywords
- For each agent in registry, sum `skill.score × skill.hits` for keywords that appear in `Object.keys(rec.skills)`  
- Normalize, return ranked list with `{ agentId, name, score, matchedSkills[], department, level }`
- File: new `src/routes/dispatch.js` (~50 lines), registered in `src/server.js`

### Frontend — Dispatch bar on Agents page

- Input: text field "Describe your task..."
- On submit: `GET /api/dispatch/recommend?q=...`
- Shows top 3-5 agent cards with: name, department badge, score bar, matched skills chips, "Open" button → navigate to agent editor, "Run in Playground" button → navigate to `/playground?agent=<id>`
- No new page needed — inline panel in AllAgents

**New API function:** `getDispatchRecommendation(q: string)` in `client/src/lib/api.ts`

---

## Phase 3 — Pipeline Templates (second highest ROI)

**What:** 5 pre-built orchestration DAGs accessible from the Orchestration page via a "Templates" button. One click loads a complete pipeline. You only fill in the task brief.

**Why it matters:** Currently every pipeline is built from scratch in the visual editor. Templates remove the wiring work for the 5 most common workflows.

### Backend

- Add `GET /api/orchestrations/templates` → returns array of template definitions
- Templates stored as JSON constants in `src/routes/orchestrations.js` (no DB needed — they're static)
- Each template: `{ id, name, description, icon, nodes[], edges[] }` — same shape as saved orchestrations so loading is trivial

- Add "Templates" button to `client/src/pages/Orchestration.tsx` header (next to "New Pipeline")
- Opens a modal grid of 5 template cards (name, description, agent chain preview)
- Click → loads template nodes/edges into the ReactFlow canvas → user adds task brief → run
- Reuse existing `setNodes`/`setEdges` state setters already in Orchestration.tsx

| MODIFY | `client/src/pages/AllAgents.tsx` — add dispatch panel |
| MODIFY | `src/routes/orchestrations.js` — add templates endpoint |
| MODIFY | `client/src/pages/Orchestration.tsx` — add templates button + modal |
| RUN | `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs harvest --write` |

---

# Knowledge Graph — Polyglot Agent Intelligence Map

## Context

User wants to implement Graphify's knowledge graph concepts into Polyglot. Graphify turns files into interactive, queryable knowledge graphs with clustering, confidence-scored edges, and physics-based vis.js visualization.

Polyglot already has:
- Full agent graph data via `/api/org-chart` (nodes + edges, all metadata)
- `@xyflow/react` installed and used in an existing OrgChart page
- Skill manifests in agent frontmatter (`skills: [{id, path, lines}]`)
- Computed skill scores in registry (`{ react: { score, hits } }`)
- Org registry with departments, phases, reportsTo hierarchy, levels, tiers

## What we're building

A new **Knowledge Graph page** (`/knowledge-graph`) — a force-directed interactive graph of the entire agent workforce showing:

1. **Agent ↔ Agent edges** (reportsTo hierarchy — already in `/api/org-chart`)
2. **Agent ↔ Skill edges** (from `frontmatter.skills[]` manifest — what skills each agent owns)
3. **Agent ↔ Agent skill-overlap edges** (inferred — agents sharing skill domains get a dashed "collaborates" edge)
4. **Clustering by department** (colored node groups matching existing department colors)
5. **Confidence tagging on edges** — EXTRACTED (solid, reportsTo), INFERRED (dashed, skill overlap)

## Data model (Graphify-inspired)

### Nodes
```typescript
interface GraphNode {
  id: string                    // agent filename (e.g. "rex") or skill id (e.g. "skill:billing")
  type: 'agent' | 'skill'
  label: string                 // display name
  department: string | null
  departmentColor: string
  community: number             // department index (0=largest), used for color
  level: number | null          // agent level 0-6
  tier: string | null
  status: string | null
  degree: number                // computed: number of edges
  metadata: Record<string, unknown>
}
```

### Edges
```typescript
interface GraphEdge {
  id: string
  source: string
  target: string
  relation: 'reports_to' | 'owns_skill' | 'skill_overlap'
  confidence: 'EXTRACTED' | 'INFERRED'
  confidence_score: number      // 1.0 = EXTRACTED, 0.5-0.8 = INFERRED
  dashed: boolean               // INFERRED → dashed
}
```

## Architecture

### Backend — one new endpoint

**`GET /api/knowledge-graph`**

Returns pre-computed graph JSON:
```json
{
  "nodes": [...],
  "edges": [...],
  "stats": {
    "totalNodes": 30,
    "totalEdges": 145,
    "byConfidence": { "EXTRACTED": 29, "INFERRED": 116 },
    "communities": 6
  },
  "departments": {...}
}
```

Logic (all in-process, no new dependencies):
1. Load all agents via `listAgents(CLAUDE_DIR/agents)`
2. Load org registry (`orgMod.loadRegistry()`)
3. Load departments (`orgMod.loadDepartments()`)
4. Build agent nodes from merged data
5. Build EXTRACTED edges from `reportsTo` fields
6. Build INFERRED `owns_skill` edges from `frontmatter.skills[]` + registry `skills` scores
7. Build INFERRED `skill_overlap` edges: for each pair of agents sharing ≥2 skill domains (from registry.skills keys), add an edge with `confidence_score = jaccard_similarity`
8. Compute degree per node
9. Assign community index = department order (by size desc, matching Graphify's 0=largest)

### Frontend — new page

**`client/src/pages/KnowledgeGraph.tsx`**

Uses `@xyflow/react` (already installed — no new deps) with a custom layout:
- **Nodes**: custom `AgentGraphNode` and `SkillGraphNode` React Flow node types
- **Layout**: `dagre` or simple force simulation via built-in React Flow `fitView` — **no D3 or vis.js needed**
- **Sidebar**: search, node inspector (click to show metadata), filter panel
- **Filters**: by department, tier, confidence level, edge type
- **Toggle**: show/hide skill nodes (declutter view)

### UI features (matching Graphify's key interactions)

| Feature | Implementation |
|---|---|
| Node color by community/dept | `departmentColor` from existing dept data |
| Edge style by confidence | solid = EXTRACTED, dashed = INFERRED |
| Click to inspect | React Flow `onNodeClick` → sidebar panel |
| Search | filter nodes by label, highlight matches |
| Department filter | toggle entire dept cluster visibility |
| Edge confidence filter | slider or toggle to hide INFERRED edges |
| Export | `html-to-image` (already in package.json) |
| Stats panel | extracted/inferred counts, god nodes (highest degree) |
| "God nodes" highlight | nodes with degree > avg+2σ get larger size |

## Critical files to create/modify

| Action | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Create | `client/src/pages/KnowledgeGraph.tsx` | New page (~450 lines) |
| Modify | `src/server.js` | Add `GET /api/knowledge-graph` endpoint (~80 lines) |
| Modify | `client/src/lib/api.ts` | Add `getKnowledgeGraph()` fetch function + types |
| Modify | `client/src/App.tsx` | Add `/knowledge-graph` route |
| Modify | `client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` | Add nav link (Network icon) |

## Node layout strategy

React Flow doesn't have built-in force simulation. Options:
1. **Dagre layout** — already used in OrgChart page, produces hierarchical layout. Good for reportsTo tree.
2. **Manual force positions** — compute x/y server-side using a simple repulsion loop, return as node positions.
3. **ELK layout** (elkjs) — installed? Check. If not, use dagre.

**Decision**: Use dagre for the base layout (hierarchy) + group nodes by department into "swim lanes". This is deterministic, matches Graphify's community clustering concept, and requires zero new packages.

Dagre is already used in OrgChart — reuse the same `getLayoutedElements()` helper pattern.

## Verification

1. `GET /api/knowledge-graph` returns valid JSON with nodes, edges, stats
2. Page loads at `/knowledge-graph` with no TypeScript errors
3. All agents appear as nodes
4. `reportsTo` edges are solid (EXTRACTED)
5. Skill overlap edges are dashed (INFERRED)
6. Clicking a node shows inspector panel with metadata
7. Department filter hides/shows clusters correctly
8. Search highlights matching nodes
9. "Hide skill nodes" toggle removes skill node layer cleanly
10. Export button downloads PNG via html-to-image

## What we're NOT building (out of scope for v1)

- Skill-to-skill semantic similarity (requires LLM/embeddings)
- SHA256 caching (agents already cached in server.js _agentCacheFull)
- File watching for graph (already handled by agent cache invalidation)
- PDF/image/video ingestion (Polyglot is agent management, not general file corpus)
- MCP server for graph queries (future)
- Neo4j/GraphML export (future)

# Cleanup + High-Value Features Plan

## Context

Goal: mass autonomous software production with low token use, no quality compromise.
Current state: Polyglot has solid infrastructure but it's cluttered with dead pages, unused server routes wired to nothing, and the highest-leverage features (smart dispatch, pipeline templates) are either server-side dead code or completely missing.

This plan removes dead weight and adds the 3 highest-ROI features in order.

---

## Phase 1 — Remove dead weight (no-risk, immediate)

### 1A. Remove `HowItWorks` page
- **Why:** 636 lines, reachable only via CommandPalette, zero functional value. It's a tutorial nobody reads.
- **Files:**
  - Delete `client/src/pages/HowItWorks.tsx`
  - Remove import + route from `client/src/App.tsx` (line 30 import, line 74 route `/how-it-works`)
  - Remove from `client/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx` line 56

- **Why:** 849 lines of pure visualization, zero dispatch, zero token savings, zero production value. The same org/dept info is already in OrgChart. We just built it but it solves no real problem.
- **Files:**
  - Delete `client/src/pages/KnowledgeGraph.tsx`

  - Remove nav link + `Network` icon import from `client/src/components/Sidebar.tsx`

### 1C. Compact the 2 over-budget agents
- **Why:** `harvest.md` (183 lines, active cron agent) and any audit stub are burning tokens on every load.
- **Action:** Run `node scripts/compactor/compact.mjs harvest --write` from project root. Check for `audit-2026-04-11.md` — if it's a dated memo not a real agent, delete it from `~/.claude/agents/`.
